nodes.label: Identity Resolution
nodes.rationale: SSO claims and group membership provide the principals used to construct query-time ACL filters.

nodes.label: Query-Time ACL Filtering
nodes.rationale: Permission filtering must happen before retrieval results reach answer synthesis, so unauthorized content is never exposed to the LLM.

nodes.label: Deny-by-Default Policy
nodes.rationale: Documents without ACL metadata are quarantined or omitted to prevent accidental exposure.

nodes.label: Mode A Strict Local-Only
nodes.rationale: Use for air-gapped, regulated, or data-residency-sensitive customers where nothing may leave the network.

nodes.label: Mode B Azure-Native
nodes.rationale: Use for Azure and M365 customers that accept managed cloud services and want faster deployment.

nodes.label: Content Hashing Skip Logic
nodes.rationale: Chunk hashes prevent re-embedding unchanged content during incremental updates.

nodes.label: Mid-Market Regulated Gap
nodes.rationale: The owned gap is regulated mid-market companies that need ACL enforcement and support but cannot justify enterprise-only platforms.

nodes.label: Pricing Recommendations by Tier
nodes.rationale: License and deployment fees scale with customer size while support costs do not scale linearly, improving margin at larger tiers.

nodes.label: Enterprise Knowledge Search Appliance
nodes.rationale: CodeSight is positioned as a consulting tool that can become an enterprise product with strict ACL enforcement and citations.

nodes.label: Design Principles
nodes.rationale: Security, pluggability, read-only behavior, deployment flexibility, and retrieval strategy selection guide product decisions.

nodes.label: LanceDB Decision
nodes.rationale: LanceDB is selected because it is embedded, file-based, supports metadata filtering, and avoids ChromaDB corruption risk.

nodes.label: Hybrid RRF Retrieval Decision
nodes.rationale: BM25 and vector search are merged with RRF because each alone misses important result classes.

nodes.label: Read-Only Invariant
nodes.rationale: CodeSight must never write to indexed repositories; writes are confined to a separate data directory.

nodes.label: Unified Consulting Repo Decision
nodes.rationale: Business operations were merged into CodeSight so consulting strategy and implementation live together.

nodes.label: Two Deployment Modes Decision
nodes.rationale: Supporting both local-only and Azure-native modes from day one preserves access to regulated and faster-moving customer segments.

nodes.label: Security-Critical Decision Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Security-critical ACL, tenant isolation, Mode A network, and data-handling changes require human approval.

nodes.label: CodeSight Client Pitch
nodes.rationale: Positions CodeSight as local, scoped AI document search for teams that need precise answers with citations without sending search data outside their network.

nodes.label: Hybrid Search
nodes.rationale: Keyword matching catches exact strings while semantic search catches meaning; RRF combines the two rankings to avoid the weaknesses of either method alone.

nodes.label: Local Privacy Model
nodes.rationale: Indexing and search run locally; only answer synthesis sends selected chunks to the configured LLM backend, and local Ollama keeps even synthesis offline.

nodes.label: Read Only Invariant Check
nodes.rationale: Bug investigation includes an explicit grep for write operations because any write to the indexed folder is treated as a critical security bug.

nodes.label: Feature Shipping Workflow
nodes.rationale: Features move through spec, tests, implementation, security checks, full suite, documentation, and selective commit to preserve engineering quality and safety.

nodes.label: Multi Model Embedding Architecture
nodes.rationale: Separate indexes per model preserve embedding-space correctness while RRF merges ranked results without comparing incompatible vector scores.

nodes.label: Same Model Index Query Constraint
nodes.rationale: Embedding vectors are meaningful only within one model's vector space, so index-time and query-time embeddings must use the same model.

nodes.label: Separate Indexes Plus RRF
nodes.rationale: Using separate code and document indexes allows domain-specific embedding models while rank-based fusion avoids raw-score calibration.

nodes.label: Query Routing Strategy
nodes.rationale: Rule-based routing avoids LLM latency while routing code symbols, semantic questions, and document keywords to appropriate indexes.

nodes.label: Chunking Strategy Research
nodes.rationale: The ranking gap is the primary problem because hit rate is already high; always-on reranking and better chunk boundaries are higher leverage than late chunking.

nodes.label: AST Based Chunking
nodes.rationale: AST chunking is validated for code retrieval, but gains depend on the embedding model and can collapse with weak generic embeddings.

nodes.label: Cross Encoder Reranker
nodes.rationale: Since the correct answer is usually in the top ten, reranking is the most direct way to move relevant results to rank one.

nodes.label: Late Chunking No Go
nodes.rationale: Late chunking has no code-specific evidence and requires model capabilities incompatible with the current local sentence-transformers setup.

nodes.label: Parent Child Chunking
nodes.rationale: Small chunks improve retrieval precision, while parent expansion supplies enough surrounding context for accurate answer generation.

nodes.label: Reranker Query Expansion Research
nodes.rationale: Voyage rerank-2.5 is supported as the default managed reranker choice, but LLM query expansion should be replaced by vector pseudo relevance feedback for default use.

nodes.label: LLM VPRF
nodes.rationale: Vector pseudo relevance feedback modifies embeddings using top results, avoiding hallucinated query text while adding only minimal latency.

nodes.label: LLM Query Expansion
nodes.rationale: Default multi-query expansion is rejected because it can degrade internal-code retrieval, add substantial latency, and be neutralized after reranking.

nodes.label: Core Search Engine
nodes.author: Juan Martinez
nodes.rationale: Core search solves scattered-document retrieval through a local hybrid index, a Python API, CLI, and web chat UI.

nodes.label: BM25 Vector RRF Pipeline
nodes.author: Juan Martinez
nodes.rationale: BM25 handles exact terms, vector search handles semantic matches, and RRF merges their rankings into final search results.

nodes.label: Read Only Invariant
nodes.author: Juan Martinez
nodes.rationale: The indexed folder is strictly read-only; search and indexing may write only to the local index data directory.

nodes.label: Embedding Model Configuration
nodes.author: Juan Martinez
nodes.rationale: Configurable embedding models improve retrieval quality while preserving local-first defaults and allowing optional API embeddings.

nodes.label: Incremental Refresh
nodes.author: Juan Martinez
nodes.rationale: Refresh should process only changed, new, and deleted files so large document folders update in seconds rather than minutes.

nodes.label: Tree Sitter Chunking
nodes.author: Juan Martinez
nodes.rationale: Tree-sitter replaces fragile regex boundaries with AST-aligned code chunks and full scope context headers.

nodes.label: Hierarchical Chunking
nodes.author: Juan Martinez
nodes.rationale: Class, method, and nested block structure supplies scope paths that improve code retrieval without requiring full LSP semantic analysis.

nodes.label: Automatic Reindexing
nodes.author: Juan Martinez
nodes.rationale: Watch and unwatch tools are deprecated because stale-index auto-refresh and scheduled cron indexing are sufficient for consulting deployments.

nodes.label: Pluggable LLM Backend
nodes.author: Juan Martinez
nodes.rationale: A backend adapter lets ask() support Claude, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, and Ollama without changing the public Python API.

nodes.label: Cross Encoder Reranking
nodes.author: Juan Martinez
nodes.rationale: A query-time cross-encoder scores query and chunk pairs after RRF, improving precision while remaining optional for latency-sensitive deployments.

nodes.label: Docker FastAPI Deployment
nodes.author: Juan Martinez
nodes.rationale: FastAPI and Docker turn CodeSight from a local demo into a production deployment for concurrent users with authentication and persistent indexes.

nodes.label: Read Only Volume
nodes.author: Juan Martinez
nodes.rationale: Client documents are mounted at /data as read-only while the index persists separately at /index, preserving the no-write-to-source invariant.

nodes.label: CNFB Query Aware Multiplicative Filename Boost
nodes.rationale: CNFB replaces binary post-reranker filename boosting with a graded multiplicative score adjustment before reranking.
nodes.norm_label: cnfb query aware multiplicative filename boost
